title.narrative: Sustainable and Inclusive Urban Prosperity in the State of Alagoas – Phase III

description.narrative:
The goal of the project is to enhance the capacity of the State of Alagoas to actively engage in sustainable and inclusive urban policies and programming leading to urban prosperity, through developing a better understanding of the urban reality, and the formulation of public policies, plans, and actions that will result in the improvement of quality of life in the cities of the State. The overall objective is the improvement of urban sustainability and living conditions of municipalities of Alagoas – in particular Maceió.
The State of Alagoas is the second smallest (27,848 km²) amongst Brazil's 27 federal states. Located in the Northeast, it has approximately 3,350,000 inhabitants and is comprised of 102 municipalities. Maceió is the capital and accounts for almost one third of the State population (1,021,709 persons estimated in 2016), with a density of 1,854 inhabitants per km².
In the capital, Maceió, roughly 25% of the population (250,000 inhabitants) lives in slums and informal settlements locally known as “grotas”. There are 100 ‘grotas' spread throughout the city, which lack tenure security and are deprived of basic infrastructure and public services. This critical situation demonstrates the daunting need for adequate housing as formulated by the international instruments on the right to adequate housing. In terms of human safety, the city has high rates of criminality, with an average of 5 homicides per day. Constant discourses from the authorities and the media call for a safer city and improved coexistence.
The program activities will benefit the overall urban population of Alagoas but will focus mainly on public authorities and officials who are accountable to design and implement policies and programmes that will meet the needs of urban dwellers. Key stakeholders from the community, private and academic sectors that are partners of the government will also benefit from the project. Ultimately, because of the focus on the ‘Grotas', slum dwellers of Maceió will also directly benefit from this project through demonstration projects in informal areas.
It should be noted that the majority of the outputs of the first phase consisted in producing diagnoses and strategies relating to various urban aspects of the capital of the state of Alagoas, Maceio, and also capacity development initiatives such as workshops and executive-courses. One exception should be mentioned, namely the incorporation of four other municipalities into the study on the development of local tourism in the state of Alagoas.
In the second phase, the project consisted in giving a logical follow-up to the diagnoses and strategies defined in the first phase. Succinctly, the second phase could summarize as (1) using qualified data and information in order to have a better understanding of the state of Alagoas territory (while the first Phase focused in calculating the basic CPI in the capital Maceió) ; (2) producing action plans following strategies previously defined; (3) profiling a new vulnerable neighborhood of Maceió, as performed during Phase 1 in 100 informal settlements; (4) providing concrete support to vulnerable populations; (5) strengthening the individual and institutional capacities of public institutions at city and state levels.
In the next phase, the third one, the project aim is to enhance State of Alagoas engagement toward sustainable and inclusive urban prosperity, through the establishment or improvement of its public policies, plans, and actions. The overall objective is the improvement of urban sustainability and living conditions of municipalities of Alagoas.
This project shall be an integrated intervention comprised of multiple components that would increase knowledge of the urban, economic, environmental and social situation of Alagoas and create the conditions and capacities for the formulation of strategies and public policies to (1) better respond to the current urban challenges, and (2) improve actions and investments in the cities, with a special focus on the grotas in the capital, Maceió.
The use of UN-Habitat methodologies and tools in the following areas shall be the entry points: housing and slum upgrading, land tenure and security, safer cities and public spaces, urban economy, municipal finance, and urban information and data.
A comprehensive continuity of the capacity development plan of the second phase will be developed and implemented, to unveil gaps in knowledge, skills, know-how and competencies related to thematic areas of urban development.
The results of deploying the data collection tools in the two previous phases will help nurture data collection and analysis and further identify policy shortcomings and problem areas where capacity need to be strengthened amongst the labor force of civil servants and other key stakeholders.
